cases.title: Uses the obstacle corner instead of the hit point

expected_feedback.diagnosis: The approach ends at the specified hit point on the obstacle edge, but the calculation uses a rectangle corner instead.
debugging_steps: Identify the named hit point in the route.
Use the distance helper with the actual segment endpoints.
expected_feedback.socratic_question: Which point does the route identify as the robot's first contact with the obstacle?

hint_ladder.hint: Find the route's explicitly named first-contact point.
The hit point lies on an edge and is not the lower-left corner.

cases.instructor_notes: Draft geometry misconception; instructor review is required.

cases.title: Uses the full rectangle instead of the traveled boundary route

expected_feedback.diagnosis: The code measures the full rectangle perimeter, but the specified route travels only from H through A and B to L. The final segment must also begin at L.
debugging_steps: List the exact route points in order.
Measure only the three boundary segments actually traveled.
Start the final segment at the named leave point.
expected_feedback.socratic_question: Which rectangle edges and partial edges does H -> A -> B -> L actually traverse?

hint_ladder.hint: Trace only the named H -> A -> B -> L route.
The robot does not travel the upper or side edges outside that route.
Add H-to-A, A-to-B, and B-to-L, then continue from L.

cases.title: Total path double-counts the obstacle approach

expected_feedback.diagnosis: One segment is included twice in the total path.
debugging_steps: Map every addend to that list.
Remove any addend without a distinct traveled segment.
expected_feedback.socratic_question: Which physical movement does the final repeated term represent?

hint_ladder.hint: Label each addend with the path segment it represents.
Two addends currently describe the same movement.
The approach-distance variable should appear only once in the total.

cases.title: Runs successfully but reads module-level points instead of parameters
cases.student_code:
def calculate_bug_route(start, hit, corner_a, corner_b, leave, goal):
    distance_to_obstacle = calculate_distance(start_point, hit_point)
    return distance_to_obstacle

start_point = (0, 0)
hit_point = (4, 0)

expected_feedback.diagnosis: The program runs because the module-level points exist, but the function ignores its own parameters, so other input scenarios give wrong results.
debugging_steps: Compare the names used inside the function with its parameter list.
Try the function with a different start and hit point.
expected_feedback.socratic_question: If a test calls the function with different points, which values does your calculation use?

hint_ladder.hint: Check which names the approach-distance calculation reads.
The function must work for every set of points passed to it.
Use the start and hit parameters inside the function body.
